title: Average Salary Excluding the Minimum and Maximum Salary
approach_name: Subtract min and max from total
notes:
Task and constraints: Return the average salary after excluding the minimum and maximum values.
Idea: Accumulate the salary total while tracking the minimum and maximum, then divide the total after removing both extrema by `salary.length-2`.
Technique and why it applies: Tracking sum and extrema in one pass avoids sorting when only the trimmed average is needed.
Invariant: The running total, `min`, and `max` summarize all values seen; the final numerator excludes one minimum and one maximum.
Edge cases: At least three salaries are guaranteed; arithmetic must preserve fractional averages; if minimum and maximum coincide, one occurrence of each is still excluded.
Complexity: O(n) time and O(1) auxiliary space.
code:
class Solution:
 def average(self,salary):return (sum(salary)-min(salary)-max(salary))/(len(salary)-2)
complexity_reason: Tracking sum and extrema in one pass avoids sorting when only the trimmed average is needed.

title: Average Salary Excluding the Minimum and Maximum Salary
approach_name: Subtract min and max from total
notes:
Task and constraints: Return the average salary after excluding the minimum and maximum values.
Idea: Accumulate the salary total while tracking the minimum and maximum, then divide the total after removing both extrema by `salary.length-2`.
Technique and why it applies: Tracking sum and extrema in one pass avoids sorting when only the trimmed average is needed.
Invariant: The running total, `min`, and `max` summarize all values seen; the final numerator excludes one minimum and one maximum.
Edge cases: At least three salaries are guaranteed; arithmetic must preserve fractional averages; if minimum and maximum coincide, one occurrence of each is still excluded.
Complexity: O(n) time and O(1) auxiliary space.
code: class Solution { public double average(int[] salary){int sum=0,min=Integer.MAX_VALUE,max=Integer.MIN_VALUE;for(int x:salary){sum+=x;min=Math.min(min,x);max=Math.max(max,x);}return (double)(sum-min-max)/(salary.length-2);} }
complexity_reason: Tracking sum and extrema in one pass avoids sorting when only the trimmed average is needed.

title: Path Crossing
notes:
Task and constraints: Return true if a path of N/S/E/W moves revisits any coordinate, including the starting point.
Idea: Start at `(0,0)`, update coordinates for each direction, and use a set of visited coordinates to detect a repeated location.
Technique and why it applies: A visited-coordinate set detects the first revisited point regardless of the route's shape.
Invariant: The set contains every position visited before the current step, including the starting point; failure to insert a new position means a crossing.
Edge cases: An empty path does not cross; returning to the origin counts as a revisit; coordinate keys must distinguish ordered pairs.
Complexity: O(n) expected time and O(n) space.
complexity_reason: A visited-coordinate set detects the first revisited point regardless of the route's shape.

Idea: Start at `(0,0)`, update coordinates for each direction, and use a set of visited coordinates to detect a repeated location.

Invariant: The set contains every position visited before the current step, including the starting point; failure to insert a new position means a crossing.
Edge cases: An empty path does not cross; returning to the origin counts as a revisit; coordinate keys must distinguish ordered pairs.
Complexity: O(n) expected time and O(n) space.
code:
import java.util.*;
class Solution { public boolean isPathCrossing(String path){int x=0,y=0;Set<String>s=new HashSet<>();s.add("0,0");for(char c:path.toCharArray()){if(c=='N')y++;else if(c=='S')y--;else if(c=='E')x++;else x--;String k=x+","+y;if(!s.add(k))return true;}return false;} }
complexity_reason: A visited-coordinate set detects the first revisited point regardless of the route's shape.

title: Can Make Arithmetic Progression From Sequence
notes:
Task and constraints: Return true if the array can be rearranged into an arithmetic progression.
Idea: Sort the array and compare every adjacent difference with the difference between the first two sorted values.
Technique and why it applies: Sorting fixes the only possible progression order, after which equal adjacent differences verify it.
Invariant: A sorted arithmetic progression has a constant adjacent difference; any mismatch proves no rearrangement can satisfy the progression.
Edge cases: The array has at least two values under constraints; duplicates are valid only if the common difference is zero.
Complexity: O(n log n) time and O(1) auxiliary space apart from sort implementation.
complexity_reason: Sorting fixes the only possible progression order, after which equal adjacent differences verify it.

Technique and why it applies: Sorting fixes the only possible progression order, after which equal adjacent differences verify it.
Invariant: A sorted arithmetic progression has a constant adjacent difference; any mismatch proves no rearrangement can satisfy the progression.
Edge cases: The array has at least two values under constraints; duplicates are valid only if the common difference is zero.
Complexity: O(n log n) time and O(1) auxiliary space apart from sort implementation.
code:
import java.util.*;
class Solution { public boolean canMakeArithmeticProgression(int[] arr){Arrays.sort(arr);int d=arr[1]-arr[0];for(int i=2;i<arr.length;i++)if(arr[i]-arr[i-1]!=d)return false;return true;} }
complexity_reason: Sorting fixes the only possible progression order, after which equal adjacent differences verify it.

title: Number of Good Pairs
notes:
Task and constraints: Return the number of index pairs i<j where nums[i] equals nums[j].
Idea: For each value, add its number of previous occurrences to the answer, then increment that value's frequency.
Technique and why it applies: Adding the prior frequency counts every pair ending at the current index exactly once.
Invariant: When a value appears for the j-th time, it forms one new good pair with each of its previous j-1 occurrences.
Edge cases: Repeated values contribute multiple pairs; first occurrences add zero; each index pair is counted once.
Complexity: O(n) expected time and O(n) space.
complexity_reason: Adding the prior frequency counts every pair ending at the current index exactly once.

Edge cases: Repeated values contribute multiple pairs; first occurrences add zero; each index pair is counted once.
Complexity: O(n) expected time and O(n) space.
code:
import java.util.*;
class Solution { public int numIdenticalPairs(int[] nums){Map<Integer,Integer>m=new HashMap<>();int ans=0;for(int x:nums){ans+=m.getOrDefault(x,0);m.put(x,m.getOrDefault(x,0)+1);}return ans;} }
complexity_reason: Adding the prior frequency counts every pair ending at the current index exactly once.

title: Shuffle String
approach_name: Place each character at its indexed destination
notes:
Task and constraints: Reconstruct a string by placing s[i] at result[indices[i]].
Idea: Allocate an output array and place each input character `s[i]` at destination `indices[i]`, then join the positions.
Technique and why it applies: Direct destination placement applies the given permutation without sorting or swapping characters.
Invariant: After placement, each output index receives the character whose permutation entry names that destination.
Edge cases: The indices form a permutation with no duplicate destinations; empty strings produce empty output.
Complexity: O(n) time and O(n) space.
complexity_reason: Direct destination placement applies the given permutation without sorting or swapping characters.

Edge cases: The indices form a permutation with no duplicate destinations; empty strings produce empty output.
Complexity: O(n) time and O(n) space.
code: class Solution { public String restoreString(String s,int[] indices){char[]out=new char[s.length()];for(int i=0;i<s.length();i++)out[indices[i]]=s.charAt(i);return new String(out);} }
complexity_reason: Direct destination placement applies the given permutation without sorting or swapping characters.

title: Count Good Triplets
notes:
Task and constraints: Count triplets i<j<k satisfying all three absolute-difference limits.
Idea: Enumerate indices `i<j<k`, prune a pair when `abs(arr[i]-arr[j])>a`, and count the triple only when both remaining difference limits pass.
Technique and why it applies: Checking all ordered index triples is direct and respects each of the three independent difference bounds.
Invariant: The loops enforce index order and the three absolute-difference constraints before incrementing the answer.
Edge cases: Values may be negative; strict index ordering avoids repeated permutations of the same triplet.
Complexity: O(n³) worst-case time and O(1) auxiliary space.
complexity_reason: Checking all ordered index triples is direct and respects each of the three independent difference bounds.

title: Count Good Triplets
notes:
Task and constraints: Count triplets i<j<k satisfying all three absolute-difference limits.
Idea: Enumerate indices `i<j<k`, prune a pair when `abs(arr[i]-arr[j])>a`, and count the triple only when both remaining difference limits pass.
Technique and why it applies: Checking all ordered index triples is direct and respects each of the three independent difference bounds.
Invariant: The loops enforce index order and the three absolute-difference constraints before incrementing the answer.
Edge cases: Values may be negative; strict index ordering avoids repeated permutations of the same triplet.
Complexity: O(n³) worst-case time and O(1) auxiliary space.
code: class Solution { public int countGoodTriplets(int[] arr,int a,int b,int c){int ans=0;for(int i=0;i<arr.length;i++)for(int j=i+1;j<arr.length;j++)if(Math.abs(arr[i]-arr[j])<=a)for(int k=j+1;k<arr.length;k++)if(Math.abs(arr[j]-arr[k])<=b&&Math.abs(arr[i]-arr[k])<=c)ans++;return ans;} }
complexity_reason: Checking all ordered index triples is direct and respects each of the three independent difference bounds.

title: Matrix Diagonal Sum
notes:
Task and constraints: Return the sum of the primary and secondary diagonals of a square matrix without double-counting the center.
Idea: For each row index `i`, add `mat[i][i]` and `mat[i][n-1-i]`, then subtract the center once when `n` is odd.
Technique and why it applies: Adding both diagonal positions per row and correcting the odd center prevents double counting.
Invariant: The accumulator contains both diagonals, with the shared center corrected exactly once for odd dimensions.
Edge cases: For even n the diagonals do not share a cell; for odd n the center would otherwise be counted twice.
Complexity: O(n) time and O(1) space.
complexity_reason: Adding both diagonal positions per row and correcting the odd center prevents double counting.

title: Matrix Diagonal Sum
notes:
Task and constraints: Return the sum of the primary and secondary diagonals of a square matrix without double-counting the center.
Idea: For each row index `i`, add `mat[i][i]` and `mat[i][n-1-i]`, then subtract the center once when `n` is odd.
Technique and why it applies: Adding both diagonal positions per row and correcting the odd center prevents double counting.
Invariant: The accumulator contains both diagonals, with the shared center corrected exactly once for odd dimensions.
Edge cases: For even n the diagonals do not share a cell; for odd n the center would otherwise be counted twice.
Complexity: O(n) time and O(1) space.
code: class Solution { public int diagonalSum(int[][] mat){int n=mat.length,ans=0;for(int i=0;i<n;i++)ans+=mat[i][i]+mat[i][n-1-i];if(n%2==1)ans-=mat[n/2][n/2];return ans;} }
complexity_reason: Adding both diagonal positions per row and correcting the odd center prevents double counting.

title: Special Positions in a Binary Matrix
notes:
Task and constraints: Count cells containing 1 whose row and column each contain exactly one 1.
Idea: Compute the sum of each row and column, then count cells equal to one whose row sum and column sum both equal one.
Technique and why it applies: Row and column sums certify whether a one is isolated along both dimensions.
Invariant: A qualifying cell is the sole one in its row and also the sole one in its column.
Edge cases: Only binary matrices are expected; rows or columns with multiple ones disqualify all their cells.
Complexity: O(mn) time and O(m+n) space.
complexity_reason: Row and column sums certify whether a one is isolated along both dimensions.

title: Special Positions in a Binary Matrix
notes:
Task and constraints: Count cells containing 1 whose row and column each contain exactly one 1.
Idea: Compute the sum of each row and column, then count cells equal to one whose row sum and column sum both equal one.
Technique and why it applies: Row and column sums certify whether a one is isolated along both dimensions.
Invariant: A qualifying cell is the sole one in its row and also the sole one in its column.
Edge cases: Only binary matrices are expected; rows or columns with multiple ones disqualify all their cells.
Complexity: O(mn) time and O(m+n) space.
code: class Solution { public int numSpecial(int[][] mat){int m=mat.length,n=mat[0].length;int[]r=new int[m],c=new int[n];for(int i=0;i<m;i++)for(int j=0;j<n;j++){r[i]+=mat[i][j];c[j]+=mat[i][j];}int ans=0;for(int i=0;i<m;i++)for(int j=0;j<n;j++)if(mat[i][j]==1&&r[i]==1&&c[j]==1)ans++;return ans;} }
complexity_reason: Row and column sums certify whether a one is isolated along both dimensions.

title: Design Parking System
approach_name: Track remaining spaces by car type
notes:
Task and constraints: Implement ParkingSystem(big, medium, small) and addCar(carType), returning true only when a matching space remains.
Idea: Store remaining spaces by car type; `addCar` returns false when that type's count is zero, otherwise decrements the count and returns true.
Technique and why it applies: A per-type capacity array makes each parking request a constant-time check and update.
Invariant: Each count equals the unused capacity for its corresponding type after all successful additions.
Edge cases: Car types map to their fixed array slots; failed parking attempts do not decrement capacity.
Complexity: O(1) time per operation and O(1) space.
complexity_reason: A per-type capacity array makes each parking request a constant-time check and update.

Edge cases: Car types map to their fixed array slots; failed parking attempts do not decrement capacity.
Complexity: O(1) time per operation and O(1) space.
code: class ParkingSystem {private int[]left;public ParkingSystem(int big,int medium,int small){left=new int[]{0,big,medium,small};}public boolean addCar(int carType){if(left[carType]==0)return false;left[carType]--;return true;}}
complexity_reason: A per-type capacity array makes each parking request a constant-time check and update.

title: Maximum Nesting Depth of the Parentheses
notes:
Task and constraints: Return the maximum nesting depth of parentheses in a valid parentheses string.
Idea: Increment `depth` on each opening parenthesis, decrement it on each closing parenthesis, and track the largest depth reached.
Technique and why it applies: Tracking current and maximum depth measures the deepest nesting without building a stack.
Invariant: `depth` is the current nesting level, and `best` is the maximum level seen in the processed prefix.
Edge cases: The input is valid; non-parenthesis characters do not affect depth; an empty string has maximum depth zero.
Complexity: O(n) time and O(1) space.
complexity_reason: Tracking current and maximum depth measures the deepest nesting without building a stack.

title: Maximum Nesting Depth of the Parentheses
notes:
Task and constraints: Return the maximum nesting depth of parentheses in a valid parentheses string.
Idea: Increment `depth` on each opening parenthesis, decrement it on each closing parenthesis, and track the largest depth reached.
Technique and why it applies: Tracking current and maximum depth measures the deepest nesting without building a stack.
Invariant: `depth` is the current nesting level, and `best` is the maximum level seen in the processed prefix.
Edge cases: The input is valid; non-parenthesis characters do not affect depth; an empty string has maximum depth zero.
Complexity: O(n) time and O(1) space.
code: class Solution { public int maxDepth(String s){int depth=0,best=0;for(char c:s.toCharArray()){if(c=='('){depth++;best=Math.max(best,depth);}else if(c==')')depth--;}return best;} }
complexity_reason: Tracking current and maximum depth measures the deepest nesting without building a stack.
